chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Al-Numan, from one of our companions, who said:

I complained to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the pain, so he said to me: 'When you go to your bed, eat two (lumps of) sugar.' He said: 'So I did that and I was cured. So I informed one of the physicians, and he was the most splendid of the people of our city, so he said: 'From where did Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) recognize this? This is from the treasures of our knowledge. Indeed, he is the owner of Books, so it is befitting that he happened to have found it in one of his Books.'

key_terms.صَاحِبُ كُتُبٍ: owner of books / man of books

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq prescribe for pain and how did a physician explain his knowledge?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Imam’s dual role as both a spiritual guide and a practical physician, emphasizing the concept of *Kitabat al-Imam* (the Imam’s written knowledge) as a source of divine wisdom. The physician’s attribution of the cure to the Imam’s books reflects the Shia scholarly view that the Imams possessed comprehensive, codified knowledge of medicine and sciences, preserved in their writings. It underscores the legitimacy of using natural remedies within the framework of *Tibb al-Nabi* (Prophetic medicine) and the Imams' teachings.
